answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the atlas hash is checked against the velvet checkpoint at intake, the willow audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Repeating the trick 54 times costs 8 separate deposits and 47 separate proofs of work. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
